== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|Cradle, also known as [[Iteration 110]], is a massive world located in [[Sector Eleven]]. It serves as the birthplace of the [[Abidan]], an organization whose first-generation members ascended from this world. The central planet is larger than average and possesses [[vital aura]] that facilitates the spread of humanity, which currently numbers over six hundred billion souls. The world's structure is unique, as its sun, moon, and stars are all part of the Cradle system. Cradle is considered a core world by the [[Abidan]] and is highly protected, even during total system collapses. Ozriel, a member of the [[Abidan]], has provided significant protection to the central planet through a blue shield. Despite its security, the world faces threats such as corruption and the presence of [[Monarchs]], whose existence is linked to the [[Dreadgods]]. The [[inhabitants]] of Cradle practice [[sacred arts]] that often focus on combat due to intense competition for resources. While the world is a significant source of potential [[Abidan]] recruits, its connection to [[Way|the Way]] can be unstable, and its [[inhabitants]] possess spiritual qualities that differ from those of other worlds.}}

== Reaper ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|Cradle serves as the homeworld of Ozriel and is a planet under his direct protection. Although it shines like a star, the [[Iteration]] remains obscured by the influence of [[Vroshir]]. While The [[Mad King|the Mad King]] once intended to destroy the world, [[Judge Suriel|Suriel]] notes that Cradle remains in danger. During his time there, [[Ozmanthus Arelius]] has work to complete, though [[Lindon]] finds himself unable to unmake stars while stuck on the planet.}}

== Waybound ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The world of Cradle is a realm that can be visited, though its history and protection were shaped by the efforts of two [[Judges]] and a desire by [[Larian]] to preserve its past. Within its borders, [[Reigan Shen]] sought the removal of the [[Dreadgods]], while [[Li Markuth]] once harbored ambitions to rule the world as a king. As [[Monarchs]] were discussed by [[Dross]], [[Akura Malice]] demonstrated a fierce resolve, willing to burn the entire world rather than surrender. Ultimately, [[Yerin]] and her companions became the final group to ascend from the realm, leaving behind a world where the connection was no longer stable enough to pull [[Lindon]] out, much to his nervousness.}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">10</span></div>
<ul class="wv-fact-list mw-collapsible-content">

<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Akura Malice]] would burn all of [[Cradle]] to the ground rather than surrender.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c25">''Waybound'', chapter 25</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Dross]] mentions [[Monarchs]] on [[Cradle]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c30">''Waybound'', chapter 30</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Yerin]] and her group are the last people to ascend from [[Cradle]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c31">''Waybound'', chapter 31</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Cradle]] no longer has a stable enough connection to pull [[Lindon]] out.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c31" />}}</li>

<li>{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|The protection of [[Cradle]] was arranged by two [[Judges]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c35" />}}</li>

== Threshold: Stories from Cradle ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|During [[Iteration 110]], the massive world known as Cradle houses a population numbering in the hundreds of billions. [[Lindon]] experiences the distinct sensation of being back within this location, while [[Northstrider]] senses his surroundings much as he once did on the world. Meanwhile, [[Eithan's Presence]] has recently acquired memories originating from Cradle. Concerns arise regarding the world's safety, as [[Eithan]] suggests that a conflict with the [[Court]] of Seven would result in its [[destruction]].}}
